ukberi-tibyan:1-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالنَّجْمِ إِذَا هَوَى (١) مَا ضَلَّ صَاحِبُكُمْ وَمَا غَوَى (٢) وَمَا يَنْطِقُ عَنِ الْهَوَى (٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذَا هَوَى): what governs the adverb (ẓarf) is the omitted verb of the oath, i.e. "I swear by the star at the time of its setting".
It is also said that النَّجْم is the (instalment-wise) descent of the Quran, so what governs the adverb is النَّجْم itself.
And the apodosis of the oath (jawāb al-qasam) is «مَا ضَلَّ».
And (عَنِ) has its usual sense, i.e. his speech does not issue from desire. It is also said that it means the bāʾ.

ukberi-tibyan:11-15.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مَا كَذَبَ الْفُؤَادُ مَا رَأَى (١١) أَفَتُمَارُونَهُ عَلَى مَا يَرَى (١٢) وَلَقَدْ رَآهُ نَزْلَةً أُخْرَى (١٣) عِنْدَ سِدْرَةِ الْمُنْتَهَى (١٤) عِنْدَهَا جَنَّةُ الْمَأْوَى (١٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَا كَذَبَ الْفُؤَادُ): it is read without shadda, and «مَا» is its mafʿūl (object), i.e. "the heart did not belie the thing which the eye saw", or "which the heart saw".
It is also read with shadda, and the meaning is close to the first. And (تُمَارُونَهُ) means "you dispute with him". And (تَمْرُونَهُ) means "you deny him". And (نَزْلَةً) is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "another time", or "another sighting". (عِنْدَ) is an adverb (ẓarf) for رَأَى. And (عِنْدَهَا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from السِّدْرَة.
It is also read جَنَّهُ, as a verb ("covered him"); this is anomalous (shādhdh), and what is in use is أَجَنَّهُ.

ukberi-tibyan:16-18.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِذْ يَغْشَى السِّدْرَةَ مَا يَغْشَى (١٦) مَا زَاغَ الْبَصَرُ وَمَا طَغَى (١٧) لَقَدْ رَأَى مِنْ آيَاتِ رَبِّهِ الْكُبْرَى (١٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ) is an adverb of time for رَأَى.
And (الْكُبْرَى) is the mafʿūl (object) of رَأَى.
It is also said that it is a naʿt (adjective) of آيَات, and the object is omitted, i.e. "something of the signs of his Lord".

ukberi-tibyan:19-20.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَفَرَأَيْتُمُ اللَّاتَ وَالْعُزَّى (١٩) وَمَنَاةَ الثَّالِثَةَ الْأُخْرَى (٢٠)).
And (اللَّاتَ) is written with tāʾ and with hāʾ, and likewise the pause on it. The alif and lām in it and in «الْعُزَّى» are redundant (zāʾida), because both are proper names.
It is also said that they are two adjectives that came to predominate (as names), like al-Ḥārith and al-ʿAbbās, so (the article) is not redundant.
The original form of اللَّات is لَوْيَة, because it is from لَوَى يَلْوِي; the yāʾ was dropped, the wāw was vowelled with a fatḥa before it, so it was changed into alif. It is also said that it is not derived.
It is also said that it is derived from لَاتَ يَلِيتُ, so on this view the tāʾ is radical.
Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, read it with a shadda on the tāʾ. They said: he was a man who used to mix (يَلِتُّ) barley-meal and other things for the pilgrims on a stone; when he died, that stone was worshipped. And الْعُزَّى is fuʿlā from الْعِزّ ("might").
(وَمَنَاةَ) is the proper name of an idol; its alif is from yāʾ, because you say مَنَى يَمْنِي when (someone) determines; it may also be from wāw, from which comes مَنَوَانِ. And (الْأُخْرَى) is tawkīd (emphasis), because the third can only be another.

ukberi-tibyan:21-22.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَكُمُ الذَّكَرُ وَلَهُ الْأُنْثَى (٢١) تِلْكَ إِذًا قِسْمَةٌ ضِيزَى (٢٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (ضِيزَى): its original form is ضُوزَى, like طُوبَى; its first letter was given kasra, so the wāw turned into yāʾ. It is not fiʿlā in origin, because nothing of that pattern has come (as an adjective) except what Thaʿlab related of their sayings رَجُلٌ كِيصَى and مِيتَةٌ حِيكَى. Others related امْرَأَةٌ عِزْهَى and امْرَأَةٌ سِعْلَى, but what is well known is عِزْهَاةٌ and سِعْلَاةٌ. Some pronounced «ضِيزَى» with hamza.

ukberi-tibyan:23-24.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنْ هِيَ إِلَّا أَسْمَاءٌ سَمَّيْتُمُوهَا أَنْتُمْ وَآبَاؤُكُمْ مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ بِهَا مِنْ سُلْطَانٍ إِنْ يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا الظَّنَّ وَمَا تَهْوَى الْأَنْفُسُ وَلَقَدْ جَاءَهُمْ مِنْ رَبِّهِمُ الْهُدَى (٢٣) أَمْ لِلْإِنْسَانِ مَا تَمَنَّى (٢٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَسْمَاءٌ): the meaning must be "things possessing names", because of His saying, Exalted is He: (سَمَّيْتُمُوهَا), since the word "name" itself is not named.
And (أَمْ) here is disjunctive (munqaṭiʿa).

ukberi-tibyan:26-26.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَكَمْ مِنْ مَلَكٍ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ لَا تُغْنِي شَفَاعَتُهُمْ شَيْئًا . . . (٢٦)).
And (شَفَاعَتُهُمْ) is plural (in its pronoun) according to the meaning of كَمْ, not its wording; and here it [Translator's note: i.e. كَمْ] is declarative (khabariyya), in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «لَا تُغْنِي» is the khabar (predicate).

ukberi-tibyan:31-31.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ لِيَجْزِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسَاءُوا بِمَا عَمِلُوا . . . (٣١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لِيَجْزِيَ): the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to what the speech indicates, namely His saying, Exalted is He: «أَعْلَمُ بِمَنْ ضَلَّ», i.e. "He has kept record of that in order to recompense".
It is also said that it is attached to the meaning of His saying, Exalted is He: «وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ», i.e. "He has informed you of His dominion and His power …".

ukberi-tibyan:32-32.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ يَجْتَنِبُونَ كَبَائِرَ الْإِثْمِ وَالْفَوَاحِشَ إِلَّا اللَّمَمَ (٣٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِينَ يَجْتَنِبُونَ) is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of الَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا, or in the position of the nominative on the implied «هُمْ» ("they are").
And (إِلَّا اللَّمَمَ) is a disjoined exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), because اللَّمَم is the minor sin.

ukberi-tibyan:37-37.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَعِنْدَهُ عِلْمُ الْغَيْبِ فَهُوَ يَرَى أَمْ لَمْ يُنَبَّأْ بِمَا فِي صُحُفِ مُوسَى وَإِبْرَاهِيمَ الَّذِي وَفَّى (٣٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَهُوَ يَرَى) is a nominal clause occurring in the place of a verbal one; the original is "has he knowledge of the unseen, so that he sees (فَيَرَى)?"; had it come that way, it would have been accusative as the answer to the interrogative.
(وَإِبْرَاهِيمَ) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to مُوسَى.

ukberi-tibyan:38-38.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَّا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرَى (٣٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ لَا تَزِرُ): «أَنْ» is lightened from the heavy (أَنَّ), and the position of the speech is genitive as a badal (substitute) for «مَا», or nominative on the implied wording "it is that … not" (هُوَ أَنْ لَا).
And (وِزْرَ) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); it is not a maṣdar (verbal noun).

ukberi-tibyan:39-39.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَأَنْ لَيْسَ لِلْإِنْسَانِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَى (٣٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَأَنْ لَيْسَ): «أَنْ» is also lightened from the heavy (أَنَّ), and the negation contained in the meaning of لَيْسَ takes the place of the compensation (taʿwīḍ).

ukberi-tibyan:4-5.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا وَحْيٌ يُوحَى (٤) عَلَّمَهُ شَدِيدُ الْقُوَى (٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (عَلَّمَهُ) is an adjective (ṣifa) of the revelation, i.e. "he taught him it".

ukberi-tibyan:40-40.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَأَنَّ سَعْيَهُ سَوْفَ يُرَى (٤٠))
His saying, Exalted is He: (سَوْفَ يُرَى): the majority read it with ḍamma on the yāʾ, and that is the proper way, because it is the khabar (predicate) of «أَنَّ» and contains a pronoun referring back to its noun.
It has also been read with fatḥa on the yāʾ; this is weak, because it then contains no pronoun referring back to the noun of «أَنَّ», which is السَّعْي; the pronoun in it is for the hāʾ [Translator's note: i.e. the person referred to by the hāʾ of سَعْيَهُ], so the noun remains without a khabar. It is like your saying إِنَّ غُلَامَ زَيْدٍ قَامَ ("Zayd's servant — stood") while you mean that Zayd stood, so the servant has no khabar. It has been explained on the basis that the implied wording is "he will see it" (سَوْفَ يَرَاهُ), so the hāʾ refers back to السَّعْي; but this is far-fetched.

ukberi-tibyan:41-41.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ثُمَّ يُجْزَاهُ الْجَزَاءَ الْأَوْفَى (٤١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الْجَزَاءَ الْأَوْفَى) is the mafʿūl (object) of يُجْزَى; it is not a maṣdar (verbal noun), because it is described as الْأَوْفَى ("the fullest"), and that is a description of the thing given in recompense, not a description of the action.

ukberi-tibyan:48-48.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ أَغْنَى وَأَقْنَى (٤٨)).
The alif of «أَقْنَى» is changed from a wāw.

ukberi-tibyan:50-50.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَأَنَّهُ أَهْلَكَ عَادًا الْأُولَى (٥٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (عَادًا الْأُولَى): it is read with tanwīn, because عَاد is the name of the man, or of the tribe-group (al-ḥayy), with the hamza after it fully pronounced. It is also read without tanwīn, as the name of the tribe (qabīla).
It is also read with tanwīn and assimilation, and in it there are two explanations:
One: he cast the vowel of the hamza onto the lām and dropped the connective hamza before the lām; so the tanwīn met the vowelled lām and was assimilated into it, just as they said لَحْمَرُ.
[Translator's note: the second explanation is not given in the source text.]

ukberi-tibyan:51-54.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَثَمُودَ فَمَا أَبْقَى (٥١) وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ مِنْ قَبْلُ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا هُمْ أَظْلَمَ وَأَطْغَى (٥٢) وَالْمُؤْتَفِكَةَ أَهْوَى (٥٣) فَغَشَّاهَا مَا غَشَّى (٥٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَثَمُودَ) is accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. "and He destroyed Thamūd"; «مَا أَبْقَى» does not govern it because of the negative particle. Likewise «قَوْمَ نُوحٍ». It may also be conjoined to «عَادًا». (وَالْمُؤْتَفِكَةَ) is accusative by «أَهْوَى».
And (مَا غَشَّى) is a second object (mafʿūl).

ukberi-tibyan:58-58.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَيْسَ لَهَا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ كَاشِفَةٌ (٥٨)).
(كَاشِفَةٌ) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) like الْعَاقِبَة and الْعَافِيَة, i.e. "there is no removal of it apart from Allah". The implied wording may also be "it has no remover" (كَاشِفٌ), the hāʾ (tāʾ marbūṭa) being for intensiveness, as in رَاوِيَة and عَلَّامَة. And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:6-9.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ذُو مِرَّةٍ فَاسْتَوَى (٦) وَهُوَ بِالْأُفُقِ الْأَعْلَى (٧) ثُمَّ دَنَا فَتَدَلَّى (٨) فَكَانَ قَابَ قَوْسَيْنِ أَوْ أَدْنَى (٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَاسْتَوَى), i.e. "then he settled". «وَهُوَ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «بِالْأُفُقِ» is its khabar (predicate), and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «اسْتَوَى».
It is also said that it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the agent of «اسْتَوَى»; this is weak, since if it were so He, Exalted is He, would have said فَاسْتَوَى هُوَ وَهُوَ. On this view the meaning would be "the two settled on the horizon", meaning Muḥammad and Jibrīl, the blessings of Allah be upon them both. The alif of «قَابَ» is a substitute for a wāw; and «أَوْ» is for vagueness (ibhām), i.e. had an onlooker seen him, the measure of nearness would have been unclear to him.
